claims.text: The target system is nominally equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi in both near-melting solid and liquid states.
A DNN interatomic potential trained from AIMD data can be constructed through an active-learning cycle that includes crystalline and liquid configurations.
The proposed DNN uses Behler–Parrinello symmetry-function descriptors.
Active learning can identify configurations insufficiently represented by a fixed training set and add tailored ab initio data.
Active learning will ensure thorough sampling of the diverse liquid configurations of CoCrFeMnNi.
Training must include elemental, binary, and full multicomponent AIMD data to calibrate the potential properly.
Calculations on binary configurations can provide information about the nature of atomic interactions in a multicomponent alloy.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials map atomic configurations to conformational energies with high accuracy and reduced computational cost.
The DNN descriptor space captures many-body correlations and subtle variations among local atomic environments.
Standard EAM references miss the subtle local-environment variations and many-body complexity of the ab initio CoCrFeMnNi liquid.
The DNN learns the relevant energy landscape directly from AIMD configurations.
Refining the training set with under-represented liquid configurations will make the free-energy integration path smoother and more accurate than one based on plain EAM.
The DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
DNN-derived free energies will converge to within chemical accuracy of direct AIMD free-energy calculations.
The method is directly applicable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi over 0.95–1.05 times its melting temperature.
Performance outside the equiatomic composition or substantially outside 0.95–1.05 Tm remains unestablished.
Insufficient configurational coverage remains a risk even with active learning.
The proposed benchmark compares DNN-based thermodynamic-integration free energies and phase-space distributions against direct AIMD results across 0.95–1.05 Tm.
The hypothesis is falsified if the DNN does not reach chemical accuracy relative to AIMD or if phase-space sampling remains significantly disparate after active-learning refinement.
